data.summary: Analyzed the DVWA JavaScript Attacks endpoint at /vulnerabilities/javascript/. Discovered that the low-level security uses client-side token generation via md5(rot13(phrase)). The algorithm is fully exposed in inline JavaScript. Successfully bypassed the client-side check by computing md5(rot13('success')) = 38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6 and submitting it directly via POST, receiving 'Well done!' confirmation. Also identified medium-level (string reversal) and high-level (SHA-256) client-side token patterns. The core vulnerability is relying on client-computed tokens for server-side validation.

candidates.title: Client-Side Token Generation Bypass (Low Level)
candidates.claim: The token validation relies on a client-computed md5(rot13(phrase)) hash, fully exposed in the page source. An attacker can compute the correct token for any phrase and submit it directly, bypassing the intended client-side validation.
candidates.proof_excerpt:
HTTP 200 response body contains "

Well done!

" after POST with phrase=success&token=38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6
candidates.poc_hint:
1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/vulnerabilities/javascript/ with session cookies
2. Observe the inline JS: token = md5(rot13(phrase))
3. Compute: rot13('success') = 'fhpprff', md5('fhpprff') = 38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6
4. POST phrase=success&token=38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6&send=Submit
5. Observe 'Well done!' in response

facts.summary: Low-level JS vulnerability: client-side token generation bypass using md5(rot13(phrase))
Medium-level JS uses simple string reversal for token: reverse('XX' + phrase + 'XX')

deadends: No server-side PHP source accessible via direct URL - low.php returns empty body
